title: Casper and the Spire
premise: Beatrix Ashgrove, an exiled storm-caller hiding his magic behind a guild clerk's ink-stained fingers, keeps ledgers of impossible trades until the night the border wards collapse and the stars go out, stranding the mortal realm in a creeping long winter. Hunted by the law that exiled him and bound by a debt to the guild's smuggler-found-family, he must cross into the fading other realm and reforge the broken covenant between realms — a pact his own betrayal helped shatter years ago. The Spire at the world's hinge demands a price: a storm-caller's name surrendered forever. In the end, Beatrix gives up not his name but his exile, choosing to stand openly as what he is, and the covenant reforges around found family rather than blood or crown.
about_author: L. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town legal disputes before turning to fiction. They write from a drafty coastal house, aided by two cats and an unreasonable number of maps.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. A quiet night of bookkeeping at the Gilded Scale guild introduces its odd family of smugglers and Beatrix's carefully hidden storm-magic. When a client pays for 'a star, still warm,' the ledger records it — and the stars begin going out overhead. Emotional beat: cozy belonging shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Wards Falling
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The border wards shatter at midnight; cold pours through like water through a cracked dam. Guild master Ovist Sable pulls Beatrix from the rubble, and the client's payment — a shard of dead starlight — hums in the vault. Emotional beat: shock hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Law Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Wardens arrive hunting the 'exiled storm-caller' they believe broke the wards. The guild hides him, and Ovist reveals the ledger's newest entry: someone traded away the covenant itself. Emotional beat: fear of exposure met with fierce loyalty.

chapters.title: A Debt Written in Frost
chapters.summary: POV Juniper, the guild's young lockpick. Juniper discovers her own name in an old ledger page tied to the covenant — she was collateral in a trade made before she could walk. She chooses to tell Beatrix anyway. Emotional beat: betrayal transmuted into trust.

chapters.title: The Road Through White Silence
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The guild party crosses the frozen borderlands toward the Spire, pursued by Warden-Captain Hale. Beatrix uses forbidden weather-sense to find a safe path, nearly revealing himself. Emotional beat: the old exile wound reopening.

chapters.title: Inn at the Edge of the Map
chapters.summary: POV Ovist Sable. Sheltering in a last lit inn, Ovist bargains with a frost-witch for passage, paying with a guild secret. He reflects on why he collects broken people. Emotional beat: paternal guilt and tenderness.

chapters.title: Stars That Went Out Singing
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. The dead stars are not dead but caged; their song bleeds through the ice at night. Juniper realizes the covenant was a duet between realms — and one side stopped singing first. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into grief.

chapters.title: Hale
chapters.summary: POV Warden-Captain Hale. Interlude from the pursuer: Hale knew Beatrix before the exile and believes the wards' fall is Beatrix's doing. Duty wars with doubt as he finds evidence of a third party. Emotional beat: righteous certainty cracking.

chapters.title: The Hinge of the World
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The party reaches the Spire: a tower half in each realm, its doors sealed with covenant-script only a storm-caller can read. Beatrix admits aloud, to the group, what he is. Emotional beat: confession met with acceptance.

chapters.title: What Was Traded
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Inside, memory-wards replay the covenant's breaking: a spire-keeper sold the realms' pact to a hungry thing called the Unlit, and the signature countersigning the trade is Beatrix's own — coerced, years ago, during his trial. Emotional beat: shame confronting context.

chapters.title: The Unlit Below
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Descending the Spire's roots, the group meets the Unlit's herald, which offers each of them their deepest want. Juniper refuses on behalf of everyone, learning refusal is the only weapon here. Emotional beat: temptation resisted collectively.

chapters.title: Halfway House of Broken Oaths
chapters.summary: POV Ovist Sable. Trapped in a waystation between realms, the guild waits out an Unlit storm. Old guild members who abandoned Ovist appear, also stranded, and uneasy truces form. Emotional beat: reconciliation without absolution.

chapters.title: Hale Crosses the Line
chapters.summary: POV Hale. Hale catches up, arrests Beatrix mid-journey — then the Unlit takes his own wardens. Hale, saved by Beatrix's storm, defects in the only way he can: he tears up the warrant. Emotional beat: duty rewritten as choice.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Last Entry
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. In the Spire archive, Beatrix finds the old spire-keeper's final ledger entry: a plan to reforge the covenant requiring a living voice from each realm, sung together. The keeper intended Beatrix all along. Emotional beat: burden becoming purpose.

chapters.title: Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. The long winter reaches its cruelest pitch; the borderlands die, and refugees flood toward the Spire. The guild turns smuggler-logistics into rescue operations. Emotional beat: found family becoming a refuge for strangers too.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Threshold
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. At the Spire's heart, the Unlit offers Beatrix restoration of his name and homeland if he walks away. He refuses — and names the true price: the covenant must be rebuilt on willing voices, not owned ones. Emotional beat: identity claimed, not granted.

chapters.title: Voices Gathered
chapters.summary: POV Ovist Sable. The final chorus assembles: Beatrix for the exiled, Juniper for the traded, Hale for the law, Ovist for the in-between, and a freed star for the sky. Each must surrender something real. Emotional beat: trembling unity.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Climax part one: the singing begins, and the Unlit floods in to drown it. Beatrix calls a storm inside the Spire for the first time since exile, holding the dark back while the others hold the song. Emotional beat: terror mastered into power.

chapters.title: What the Dark Kept
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Climax part two: Juniper realizes the Unlit is the first spire-keeper, unmade by his own bad bargain, starving for a voice of his own. She offers him a line in the song instead of destruction. Emotional beat: mercy as the sharpest blade.

chapters.title: Covenant
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The new covenant seals — not a wall between realms but a door with obligations on both sides. Stars relight; winter breaks. Beatrix surrenders his exile-status formally, signing himself back into the world. Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Ledgers Balanced
chapters.summary: POV Hale. Aftermath: Hale testifies to overturn the exile decree; the guild faces amnesty negotiations with wry dread. Ovist opens a new ledger titled 'Possible Things.' Emotional beat: weary, earned hope.

chapters.title: Casper and the Spire
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Epilogue: Beatrix learns the star they freed has taken a name — Casper — and chosen to stay near him as a small warm light over the guildhouse. He writes the first entry of his own ledger: debts owed to family, all marked paid. Emotional beat: quiet joy, home at last.
